Employment Type: Temporary Full Time
Remuneration: As per Public Hospital Medical Officers (State) Award
Hours Per Week: 38

An exciting opportunity to join the team in the Obstetrics and Gynaecology Department at the Northern Beaches Hospital. Rewarding career opportunities are available at NSLHD and offer a flexible career with a diverse and interesting case mix where medical staff are involved in all aspects of a patient's care.

Northern Beaches Hospital

Northern Beaches Hospital provides world-class, Level 5 delineation services for both public and private patients. The hospital features 486 beds, 50 bed Emergency Department, 20 bed general and cardiothoracic ICU, 14 fully equipped theatres, including hybrid theatres, 2 cardiac catheter labs, 4 procedural rooms and a state of the art education and interactive SIM Centre.

The Northern Beaches Hospital offers the community comprehensive Women's Health services, thanks to the expertise of our midwifery, nursing and medical staff.

The Hospital's Women's Health services include the following:

Birthing services, with flexible models of pregnancy, birthing and post natal care for all patients
Midwifery Group Practice
Midwifery led care
GP Shared Care
Public and Private Obstetric Care
State of the Art Birthing Faclities, including birthing pools and immediate access to theatres and urgent care, if required
Premium maternity accommodation 
A leading standard of obstrtic and midwifery care
Diverse inpatient and outpatient maternity support, including assistance with bonding, attachment, feeding and parenting, access to Allied Health Services and access to post discharge midwifery care and community supports
A fully equipped and staffed Special Care Nursery to care for newborn babies from 32 weeks gestation
A wide range of general Gynaecology services

What you'll be doing

The primary role of the Senior Resident Medical Officer - Obstetrics and Gynaecology is to provide quality obstetric and gynaecological care to women in the labour ward, antenatal clinics and relevant patients presenting to the emergency department at The Northern Beaches Hospital.
The Senior Resident Medical Officer will, under an appropriate level of supervision, evaluate, diagnose, treat and provide consultation to female patients of all ages presenting in any condition or stage of pregnancy or the puerperium; and female patients presenting with illnesses, injuries and disorders of the gynaecological or genitourinary system.
 

THIS POSITION IS BASED AT THE NORTHERN BEACHES HOSPITAL, FRENCHS FOREST, NSW

 

 
 

 
 
 
 
 
 

 

Qualifications and experience commensurate with the Essential Requirements for the role

Demonstrated ability to work independently in a supervised environment.

Adept ability to work effectively as part of a multi-disciplinary team with an understanding of the roles of the doctor and other members of the healthcare team.

Adept written and verbal communication skills and ability to communicate effectively and respectfully with patients, family members and others members of the health care team.

Adept good organisational and time management skills and ability to manage competing priorities in a complex environment.

Demonstrated commitment to quality improvement, patient safety and risk management.

Evidence of continuing professional development and commitment to self-education.

result.description:
General Practitioner (GP) — Contract Opportunity Across Australia 

 Join a dynamic HealthTech startup and wellness centre delivering modern, patient-centred primary care through blended in-person and telehealth services. We are seeking experienced General Practitioners with full Australian registration and residency or citizenship to work on a contract basis across Australia. This role offers flexibility, strong professional support, and competitive billings-based pay of  65%–70% on billings . 

 What You’ll Do 

 
	 Provide high-quality general practice consultations to diverse adult and family populations via telehealth and in-clinic sessions. 
	 Deliver comprehensive assessments, diagnosis, management plans, acute care and chronic disease management in line with best practice guidelines. 
	 Collaborate with a multidisciplinary team including allied health, mental health clinicians, and digital health specialists to coordinate patient care. 
	 Use the HealthTech platform to document encounters, follow up results, prescribe and refer, and support continuity of care. 
	 Participate in targeted quality improvement projects, remote case reviews, and virtual clinical governance meetings. 
 

 Who You Are 

 
	 Registered with the Australian Health Practitioner Regulation Agency (AHPRA) as a General Practitioner. 
	 Australian citizen or permanent resident eligible to work across Australian states and territories. 
	 Experienced in general practice or family medicine with strong clinical decision-making and communication skills. 
	 Comfortable with telehealth platforms and digital patient records, plus the ability to balance virtual and face-to-face consultations. 
	 Committed to delivering patient-centred, evidence-based care with cultural sensitivity and respect for diverse communities. 
 

 Why Join Us 

 
	  Flexible hours:  Design a schedule that fits your lifestyle, with options for part-time or concentrated clinic blocks. 
	  Professional development:  Training provided, access to clinical upskilling, peer review, and mentorship within a growing HealthTech practice. 
	  Attractive earnings:  Competitive percentage on billings between 65% and 70% with transparent revenue sharing. 
	  Innovative environment:  Work with cutting-edge digital tools, telehealth infrastructure, and a mission-driven team focused on accessible care. 
	  Nationwide opportunities:  Contract roles available across Australia, enabling a range of practice locations and patient communities. 
 

  Ideal Candidates  

 We welcome applications from: 

 
	 GP Registrars 
	 VR GPs 
	 Non-VR GPs 
	 Doctors with previous telehealth experience 
	 Doctors seeking flexible work-from-home arrangements 
 

 Start Timeframe and Contract Details 

 Positions begin from a fixed date with contract terms tailored to clinician preference and site needs. This role is ideal for GPs seeking contractual flexibility while maintaining clinical excellence and continuity of care. The working arrangement supports clinicians who value autonomy and modern practice models.

result.description:
MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Kickstart your career in a warm, supportive environment - Welcome to Bingara!

Remuneration: $32.85 - $36.04 per hour + Superannuation + Salary Packaging + Incentives
Located in: Bingara Multipurpose Service 
Employment Type: Permanent Part Time
Hours per week: 13
Position Classification: Assist in Nursing
Requisition ID: REQ669494
Applications Close: Sunday, 1st August 2026.

To be eligible for permanent employment in this position you must be an Australian Citizen, or a permanent resident of Australia, or a New Zealand citizen with a current New Zealand Passport. Employment of a temporary visa holder may only occur if no suitable local candidate is identified for the position; in this instance, you may only be offered employment in line with the conditions and expiry date of your visa. 

We are unable to accommodate visa sponsorship for applicants requiring a visa for this position. 

About the role

The Assistant in Nursing (AIN) is responsible for providing positive health outcomes for their patients, under the guidance and direction of Registered Nurse (RN). On any given day, you will be assisting patients with medicine administration, providing patient personal cares, helping with their mobility, interacting with the Diversional Therapist to assist with activities, and so on. If you're looking to start your nursing career in a diverse, encouraging environment, look no further - Bingara is waiting for you!

You won't be working alone - you will be supported by the Senior RN's, Clinical Nurse Educator (CNE) and Health Service Manager (HSM). You will also enjoy a being part of a wider, multi-discipline team including Allied Health and Medical staff. Pursing further education and development is not only encouraged, but truly championed by a team where "growing your own" is a core value.

Requirements: 

Certificate III Assistant in Nursing or currently enrolled in an undergraduate Registered Nursing degree (completion of first year and first semester or trimester of second year), or currently enrolled in a TAFE NSW Diplomas of Nursing (completion of identified foundational units in practice AND 80 hours of clinical placement).

Why you will love working here:

Bingara, NSW offers an exceptional country lifestyle, combining a welcoming community with stunning natural surroundings and a relaxed pace of life. Residents enjoy affordable living, excellent local amenities, and easy access to outdoor activities such as fishing, hiking, and exploring nearby national parks. For professionals, Bingara provides opportunities across agriculture, tourism, small business, healthcare, education, and essential services, while offering the work-life balance that regional living is known for. It's a place where you can build a rewarding career, raise a family, and enjoy a genuine sense of community.

 

Relocating? We've Got You Covered

Making a move can feel overwhelming, but support is available.

The Welcome Experience is a free service designed to help health workers and their families settle into regional communities. From connecting you with local schools, childcare providers, sporting clubs, housing information, and community networks, the program helps make your transition smoother so you can feel at home sooner and start enjoying everything your new community has to offer.

Learn More: www.nsw.gov.au-welcomeexperience

Benefits:

You'll enjoy a range of benefits designed to support you both at work and at home, including:

 Be rewarded with up to $20,000 in the first 12 months PLUS up to $10,000 each year thereafter in fortnightly payments under the Rural Health Workforce Incentive Scheme.*
 Monthly Allocated Day Off for full-time employees
 Four weeks annual leave (pro-rata for part-time staff)
 Paid parental leave for eligible employees, supporting true balance during important life moments
 Salary packaging options up to $11,600, plus novated leasing
 Fitness Passport offering discounted gym and wellness options for you and your family
 Access to the Employee Assistance Program for confidential support for staff and their families

Need more information?

1) Click here for the Position Description
2) Find out more about applying for this position

For role-related queries or questions contact Leesa Evans | Leesa.Evans@health.nsw.gov.au

Important Information

At Hunter New England Local Health District, we are an inclusive employer dedicated to fostering a diverse, inclusive, and welcoming workplace. Our commitment to a workforce that reflects the community we care for is essential for delivering the highest quality healthcare to our community. We encourage people with diverse lived experiences to apply. If you require any accommodations or adjustments to the recruitment process please let us know when you apply or at any stage of the process. We will work with you to meet your needs and create the best possible experience. Please contact HNELHD-Diversity@health.nsw.gov.au for confidential support. 

Additional Information
